svg.title: Day 4 test-generation benchmark: end-to-end flow
svg.desc: Twelve stages from the frozen golden set to notebook 03, each naming the Python module and functions it uses and the reason the stage exists: generation (build the input, generate with gpt-6-luna, check and save the reply) then evaluation (error analysis and blind label sheets, a seeded check of the gpt-6-sol judge, scoring, comparison with the blind labels, history file, notebook).
svg.text: Day 4: AI test-generation benchmark, end-to-end flow

g.text: 1. Golden set (frozen)
datasets/testgen_golden.json
v1.0 · 10 stories · 39 ACs · 78 expected ideas · fingerprint 228e95aab97e
Why: The answer key: what a good set of tests for each story must contain.
2. Validate the golden set
python datasets/validate_testgen_golden.py
Structure checks and derivability warnings → PASS before any run
Why: Catch mistakes in the answer key before it marks anything.
3. Build the generator input
bench/golden.py → load_golden() · story_card() · load_prompt(v)
Card: ID, title, story, ACs only · fingerprints: golden, prompt, per story
Why: Give the generator the story card and nothing from the answer key.

svg.text: only the story card reaches the prompt.
ideas = what the judge marks against.

g.text: 4. Generate test cases (one call per story)
bench/generate.py → run() → generate_story() → call_generator()
OpenAI Responses API · gpt-6-luna · instructions = prompt, input = story card
Why: Produce the output under test: the system under test is the prompt.
5. Check the reply
bench/testcase_schema.py → parse_reply() · check_cases()
Strict and usable JSON · fields, case_id, technique, covers = the story's AC IDs
Why: A free check that the output is usable before paying to judge it.
6. Save the run
results/testgen/gen_<prompt>_<model>_g<golden>_r<run>_<time>.json
Raw reply, issues, tokens, latency, all fingerprints · never overwritten
Why: Keep every output, so it can be re-scored without paying to regenerate.
7. Error analysis and blind label sheets (prompt v1, run 1)
bench/review_sheet.py · bench/calibration.py build
Cases next to ideas → failure modes F1–F9, rules D1–D4 · 20 cases + 24 ideas labelled
Why: Learn how the generator fails, and label a sample before seeing any judge verdict.
8. Seeded check (gate)
python -m bench.score --seeded
Hand-made cases with known answers, incl. correct controls · judge v1 33/33, judge v2 46/46
Why: Show the judge can catch each kind of error and does not fail good work.

svg.text: Fail here → fix the judge prompts

g.text: 9. Score each story and run
bench/score.py → score_run() → judge.py judge_story()
Free: schema, claimed coverage, count · judge gpt-6-sol: correct, technique, concrete,
duplicate, verified coverage, recall · precision derived
Why: Turn each run into comparable numbers: quality, cost and time.

svg.text: Blind to v1 / v2. Recall counts

g.text: 10. Compare the judge with your blind labels
python -m bench.calibration compare <score file>
Agreement per check · confusion tables · false passes · every disagreement with its reason
Why: Show the judge agrees with an expert on real, messier cases, not just seeded ones.
11. History file
results/testgen_history.csv
One row per story per run: time, model, all fingerprints, scores, cost, seconds
Why: Track results over time and across prompt or model changes (Day 5 CI).
12. Notebook 03
03_testgen_benchmark.ipynb
v1 vs v2 over 3 runs: recall, precision, case count, cost · judge errors
Why: Answer the question: does v2 write better tests than v1, and at what cost?

svg.text: prompt v1 and v2, 3 runs each
